title: Multifunctional, Tough, and Highly Stretchable Aramid Nanofiber Reinforced Conductive Hydrogel for Wearable Electronics
authors: Qifa Gou; Yadong Chen; Jipeng Wang; Chang Wu; Longbiao Yuan; Zihao Gao; Jianmin Guo; Xuelei Wang; Li Ke; Qiang Du; Tianxing Gong; Chongshu Wang; Shibo Wei
abstract: Abstract Flexible strain sensors require stable, sensitive, and repeatable signal acquisition during complex motions, and hydrogels have emerged as promising candidates for this purpose. In this study, a fiber-reinforced ionic conductive hydrogel was constructed by introducing an aramid nanofiber (ANF) reinforcing framework and a dynamic Zn2+ coordination network. ANF enhanced stress transfer and load-bearing capacity, while reversible Zn2+ coordination crosslinks provided energy dissipation and stable ionic conductive pathways. The resulting hydrogel exhibited a tensile strength of 2.22 MPa, fracture strain of 800%, toughness of 9.58 MJ m−3, and electrical conductivity of 0.66 S m−1. Moreover, it showed reliable resistance responses to tensile and compressive stimuli, with tensile and compressive gauge factors (GF) of 6.94 and 8.4, respectively. The synergistic design of ANF reinforcement and Zn2+ coordination effectively balances mechanical performance, conductivity, and sensing sensitivity, offering a feasible strategy for flexible electronics and wearable sensors.

Blue-Hazard Free WOLEDs with High Efficiency and Color-Rendering Index by Exciton Confinement and Energy Transfer Sensitization from Bluish-Green Emitter to Ultrathin Light-Emitting Layer
authors: Haoran Yang; Lingdong Wang; Binhe Li; Guodong Sun; Chuanjiang Qin; Liang Zhou
matched_keywords: oled; organic light-emitting diode; emitting layer
abstract: Abstract White organic light-emitting diodes (WOLEDs) demonstrate tremendous potential as next-generation light sources. However, the simultaneous achievement of ideal white emission and high efficiency remains a significant challenge. This work proposes a solution by inserting low-mobility light-emitting layers (EMLs) on both sides of the high-mobility EML and introducing ultrathin red phosphorescent EMLs to regulate exciton distribution and energy transfer processes. The obtained WOLEDs achieve the maximum power efficiency and external quantum efficiency up to 77.1 lm W–1 and 32.2%, respectively, which maintain 52.8 lm W–1 and 29.5% at 1000 cd m–2. Concurrently, the devices exhibit color rendering index exceeding 80 within a luminance range from 1000 to 80000 cd m–2, accompanied by complete elimination of harmful blue emission. Time-resolved photoluminescence spectroscopy reveals that the red emission of WOLEDs based on ultrathin red EMLs mainly originates from energy transfer through the quasi-equatorial conformer of bluish-green emitter DMAC-TRZ. This work elucidates the concealed photophysical mechanisms in WOLEDs based on ultrathin EMLs while presenting a promising strategy for energy-efficient and blue-hazard free lighting technologies.

title: Solubility-driven morphological decoupling enables elastic electron-deficient semiconducting polymers for fully stretchable electronics
authors: Hayeong Park; Qian Liu; Wenhao Li; Minji Chung; Gunmo Koo; Chien-Chung Shih; Christopher R. McNeill; Dongsheng Yan; Yang Wang; Shanshan Zhou; Mandar M. Shirolkar; Ruicheng Li; Aung Ko Ko Kyaw; Yunqi Liu; Prashant Sonar; Joon Hak Oh
abstract: The development of fully stretchable electronics is limited by the scarcity of electron-deficient polymers that combine high electron mobility with mechanical elasticity. Here, we report a solubility-driven morphological decoupling strategy that mitigates this trade-off by incorporating ∼10% planar, insoluble PyF units into a semicrystalline PySe backbone. This approach yields a hierarchical morphology characterized by suppressed long-range crystallinity alongside robust local aggregation. Driven by strong fluorine (F)-sulfur (S) interactions, highly ordered face-on domains function as robust physical anchors, providing the polymer network with exceptional elasticity to reversibly dissipate stress and preserve charge percolation pathways. Consequently, the resulting terpolymer largely relieves the long-standing trade-off between charge transport and mechanical stretchability, delivering a near-unity initial electron mobility (∼1.0 square centimeter per volt per second) and retaining 0.5 square centimeters per volt per second even under 100% applied strain, representing the highest performance reported to date. To demonstrate the practical utility of this system, we fabricated stretchable ambipolar inverters and phototransistors that maintain high performance under severe deformation. Notably, the phototransistors sustain an exceptional responsivity of 15.8 amperes per watt and an external quantum efficiency exceeding 2900% at 100% strain. These results establish a powerful blueprint for intrinsically elastic semiconductors, enabling the realization of high-performance, fully deformable optoelectronic systems.

title: Monolithic tiered microlithography for stretchable multilayer electronics with high-density, soft, and ultrathin VIAs
authors: Xinjian Xie; Guangrui Ju; Xiongwei Luo; Shengwei Feng; Hongjiao Li; Yijun Zhang; Wenqian Feng
abstract: Stretchable multilayer electronics that sustain reliable electrical performance under mechanical deformation are critical for advanced skin-like devices. A remaining challenge is the development of high-density, soft, and ultrathin vertical interconnect accesses (VIAs) that enable reliable electrical interconnection in flexible and stretchable circuits, particularly at small feature sizes. Here, we present a three-dimensional (3D), tier-by-tier photolithography strategy using PEDOT-based conductors and polydimethylsiloxane (PDMS)–based insulators, each photocurable within 10 seconds, to directly pattern soft VIAs and planar interconnects across lithographically defined PDMS openings. Maskless, full-field exposure enables thousands of in-plane and through-plane electrical connections in a single step, bypassing conventional hole-by-hole fabrication and manual VIA-to-pad alignment. The multilayer stack ensures minimal thickness, matched mechanical compliance, and robust conduction and insulation, enabling soft VIAs to preserve cross-layer electrical performance. Integration of lithographically defined cutouts and perforations yields breathable, conformal bioelectronics with skin-friendliness and stable signal acquisition in wearable wireless ECG monitoring. This multilayer 3D electronics platform can be extended to biomolecular sensing in soft organs, where thin, integrated, and stretchable designs are essential.

title: Buckled Silver Microflake Conductors With In Situ‐Generated Ag–O Coordination Enable 3D‐Printed Stretchable Cardiac Bioelectrodes
authors: Luyizheng Shuai; Wenjin Guo; Xiaoyu Hu; Boren Zhou; Kaiyu Yuan; Dong Qian; Shaoli Fang; Enzhao Liu; Tong Zou; Jingzhao Lu; Jingjing Li; Xiang Zhou; Zunfeng Liu
abstract: ABSTRACT Metallic pacemaker electrodes risk myocardial injury during implantation, while silver micro‐flakes (AgMFs), despite excellent conductivity, are too rigid for stretchable devices without proper composite/device engineering. Here, we present a synergistic strategy to fabricate fully stretchable, electrically stable, and crack‐resistant cardiac electrodes by integrating AgMF‐based ink with metal‐organic interfacial bonding, biaxial buckling, and wet‐adhesive hydrogels. In situ‐generated Ag–O coordination of silver nanoparticles (AgNPs) in the polymer matrix/conductor dissipates stress and suppresses crack propagation, effectively compensating for AgMF rigidity and enabling intact buckled microstructures. The resulting electrodes exhibit high conductivity (∼2.1 × 10 4 S cm −1 ) and stable resistance under 50% cyclic strain, exceeding cardiac motion requirements (15%–20%). The ink is 3D‐printable into mesh electrodes and can be integrated with wet‐adhesive hydrogels to form puncture‐free, stretchable metallic cardiac bioelectrodes with excellent biosafety, offering a promising route toward leadless pacemakers and long‐term wireless cardiac monitoring. A multiscale synergistic strategy integrating metal‐organic interfacial bonding with stretch‐release‐induced buckled architectures enables silver microflake conductors with simultaneously high conductivity and large deformability, demonstrated for 3D printing of bioadaptive, puncture‐free cardiac electrodes and stretchable wireless coils for dynamic cardiac stimulation and long‐term electrophysiological monitoring.
